pm_exper_user_728_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How do you cope when a loss still feels just as heavy years later?
pm_exper_user_728_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Oh love, when my sibling passed all those years ago, the grief never truly vanished, but it softened. I cope by finding ways to keep them close in daily life — baking their favourite treat, revisiting places we shared — so they remain a gentle part of my present as well as my past.
(b) Oh love, losing my only brother so young left a space that never quite filled, and I still carry him with me. On quiet Sunday mornings I tend the garden and hum the old hymns he liked, letting those moments be my way of feeling close to him again.
(c) Oh love, I lost my only brother when I was quite young, and even now the weight of it can surprise me. I find it helps to keep small rituals alive — playing the old songs he loved or telling stories about him over tea with a dear friend — so his presence still feels woven into my days.
(d) Oh love, when someone dear is gone, the ache can linger for years, and that’s only natural. I find keeping small traditions, like listening to favourite music or visiting a meaningful place, can bring comfort and make the sadness a little easier to carry.
